title.value: Learning to repeatedly solve routing problems
title.justification: This is the title of the paper.
title.quote: Learning to repeatedly solve routing problems

extractions.description: The paper presents a learned heuristic for the reoptimization of a problem after a minor change in its data, specifically the capacited vehicle routing problem with static clients and changed demands. It aims to predict and fix edges of an original solution that are likely to remain in an optimal solution after demand changes, reducing complexity and speeding up resolution.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on optimizing vehicle routing, which has direct implications for reducing transportation costs and emissions, contributing to sustainable logistics.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: This is the case of applications in which the infrastructure whose operations must be optimized does not change, for example a fleet of vehicles that deliver goods or the power plants producing energy, but the demand of goods or energy changes

To provide a concrete example, let us consider the CVRP, which is the problem where
we will apply the method proposed in this paper. The goal of the CVRP is to construct
vehicle routes in order to serve geographically-dispersed clients while minimizing the
travel costs and respecting vehicle capacity

applications.value: Commercial transportation- optimize freight routing and scheduling
applications.justification: The paper focuses on optimizing vehicle routes which is directly related to freight routing and scheduling.
applications.quote:
Let us take the example of a delivery company that solves CVRPs on a daily basis. For a given day, the company observes that the clients are the same as in the instance solved the previous day (i.e., same client
locations) and that only some clients have a different demand.
